function: SNN with on-chip reward-based triplet-STDP training acts as the binary classifier inside StructNet for MIMO-OFDM symbol detection; hardware/software hybrid testbench. p. 11-12
system: MIMO-OFDM, 2 transmit and 2 receive antennas, half-wavelength ULAs; 4-PAM/8-PAM Gaussian and 16-QAM WINNER II channels; no RIS; band not stated. p. 12
method: Spiking neural network (LIF neurons) trained on-chip with reward-based triplet STDP, supervised; embedded in StructNet whose linear channel-estimation layer is trained in software. p. 6, 11-12
data_channel: Following StructNet [3]: Gaussian channel with 4-PAM/8-PAM, and WINNER II NLOS urban macrocell outdoor-to-indoor with 16-QAM; MNIST and CIFAR-10 also used for the learning rule. p. 9, 12
test_conditions: Dataset split 1992 training and 3000 test samples; separate experiments for Gaussian 4-PAM/8-PAM and WINNER II 16-QAM; SER swept over Eb/No; no cross-condition test. p. 12
baselines: Learned: pair-based STDP SNN, ADNN-GT, ADNN-LMMSE and software StructNet; RC-Struct and RC-AttStructNet-DF only in running time; no non-learned detector in SER results. p. 12-13
metrics: Symbol error rate versus Eb/No (0 to 20 dB); MNIST and CIFAR-10 error rates; running time; post-layout power, silicon area and energy per spike operation. p. 9-12
complexity: Measured running time in Table III (SNNOT with TSTDP 20.26 s, PSTDP 16.35 s) plus post-layout power 20.92 uW and area 37 x 62 um2. p. 9, 12
q1_support: p. 12: "the WINNER II channel model [50]" is used with 16-QAM in an urban macrocell NLOS outdoor-to-indoor scenario. It is a standardized model outside the listed set (see notes); the 4-PAM/8-PAM experiments use a Gaussian channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "Among them, 1992 samples were used for the training process"; the other 3000 samples are a held-out part of the same data. Gaussian and WINNER II cases are separate experiments; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 12: "are compared with purely software-based neural networks, including ADNN-GT, ADNN-LMMSE, and StructNet". All compared methods are learned (pair-based STDP is the proposed method with another rule); no LMMSE or sphere-decoding detector appears in the SER results (Fig. 16).
q4_support: p. 12: "The processing time of the introduced training neural network implementation and other Python-based symbol detection methods are compared in Table III", with SNNOT running times listed in the table; power and area are on p. 9.
q5_support: p. 12: "dataset consists of 4992 samples", following StructNet [3]; no code or data link is given. MNIST and CIFAR-10 (p. 9) are datasets of the learning task alone and do not count.
notes: Included although the paper is mainly circuit design: Section V (p. 11-13) evaluates the on-chip trained SNN as the classifier of StructNet for 2x2 MIMO-OFDM symbol detection and reports SER (Fig. 16), so area 1. q1 is marked met only through WINNER II, a standardized model not in the listed set; reviewer to confirm. q3 is 0 because every compared method is learned and no non-learned detector appears in the results; the pair-based STDP network is a variant of the proposed method. q4 rests on the measured running times of Table III. The 3GPP-3D results are in [3], not in this paper.
